sources.entry: av - Pythonic bindings for FFmpeg's libraries.

summary.one_liner: PyAV is a Pythonic binding for the FFmpeg libraries that gives direct, low-level access to media containers, streams, packets, codecs, and frames.
summary.what_it_does: PyAV exposes FFmpeg's libraries to Python with direct access to containers, streams, packets, codecs, and frames. It provides some transformations of that data and helps move data to and from other packages such as NumPy and Pillow. The README says it aims to offer FFmpeg's full power while handling many low-level details. It is aimed at users who need precise control and says that for simple tasks the ffmpeg command line may be easier. Binary wheels with FFmpeg bundled are provided on PyPI for Linux, macOS, and Windows, and conda-forge is also supported. Source builds can target an existing FFmpeg installation or a locally built one.
use_cases: decode video or audio frames in Python
read and write media containers and streams
convert frames to NumPy arrays or Pillow images
low-level control over codecs and packets
build custom media processing pipelines on FFmpeg
how_to_run: pip install av --no-binary av  (builds from source against existing FFmpeg on Linux or macOS)
git clone the repo, then: source scripts/activate.sh && ./scripts/build-deps && make && make test && pip install .
notable: Binary wheels bundle FFmpeg for Linux, macOS, and Windows
Exposes containers, streams, packets, codecs, and frames directly
Available on both PyPI and conda-forge
caveats: Building from source needs FFmpeg development files and pkg-config, and can be complex
README states the release supports FFmpeg 9.x, while the source build section mentions ffmpeg 8.x
Low-level API; the README says it is more of a hindrance than a help for simple tasks the ffmpeg command handles
keywords: work with media files in python
